inputs.prompt: Compare an English and a French version of the same document. English: {{inputs.english}}. French: {{inputs.french}}. List every difference in meaning, number, date, amount, duration or obligation as a table: Where (section or sentence) | English says | French says | Kind (meaning, number, date, obligation, omission) | Severity (low, medium, high). If the two versions agree on a point, do not list it. If a passage exists in only one version, list it as an omission. The first line of your answer is exactly this sentence: fr « Traduction automatisée non certifiée — à faire réviser par un professionnel avant tout usage, surtout pour un document juridique. » en « Automated, uncertified translation — to be reviewed by a professional before any use, above all for a legal document. » (use the one that matches the output language). Mark anything you are unsure of as « À réviser » (fr) or « To review » (en). Name the terminology source of every term you choose (the usage recommended by the Office québécois de la langue française, OQLF, and its Grand dictionnaire terminologique, when one applies; otherwise say « usage courant »). Never invent a legal term: when no established Québec term exists, keep the source term in brackets and flag the passage. Never quote a statute; refer to it by name only.

From this table of differences: {{steps.differences.content}}, write a three-line summary: how many differences, how many of high severity, and which section to review first. Do not decide which version prevails.
